target.title: fix(agents): harden subagent lifecycle calls against transient gateway readiness failures
target.body:
## Summary

- add a bounded `sessions.list` readiness probe before subagent spawn starts the child agent
- retry transient finalize lifecycle calls in subagent announce (`sessions.patch` / `sessions.delete`)
- retry transient sweep cleanup `sessions.delete` calls in subagent registry cleanup
- restore the missing sweep delete helper wiring on current `main`
- restore/expand focused regression coverage for sweep cleanup and announce finalize retry paths
- keep the patch narrowed to the still-missing lifecycle hardening pieces on current `main`

## Why this refreshed PR

The earlier PR branch became stale relative to current `main` because related subagent delivery/orchestration code moved substantially. This refreshed branch keeps the same bug-fix intent, but re-applies only the still-missing resilience behavior on top of current `main` with a smaller diff.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Root Cause

Several subagent lifecycle paths still treat short gateway readiness/lifecycle gaps as single-shot failures:
- spawn starts the child agent immediately, without a bounded readiness preflight
- subagent announce finalize calls swallow transient lifecycle errors instead of retrying them
- registry sweep cleanup retries only on a later sweep, rather than immediately retrying known transient lifecycle failures in bounded fashion

## Test Plan

- `OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=tmp/pr-74131-final-verify.json node --no-maglev ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts`

## Results

- `src/agents/subagent-registry-cleanup.test.ts` ✅
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts` ✅
- `src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts` ✅
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts` ✅
- 4/4 targeted files passed
- 41/41 targeted tests passed

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Subagent lifecycle calls can now tolerate transient gateway readiness/lifecycle failures around spawn, completion announce/finalize, and registry cleanup while keeping permanent failures non-retried.

Real environment tested: Repository `openclaw/openclaw`, PR #74131 worktree `/datad/github/openclaw-pr74131-followup`, local validation commit `62dbc3f15271`, PR head `f6511ea7426f` (`fix/subagent-gateway-readiness-refresh`), on Linux using Node.js v24.14.1. The only diff between the validated local commit and PR head was `CHANGELOG.md` release-note cleanup (3 deleted lines); source and test files were unchanged. To avoid disrupting the user's production gateway, I ran the PR build against a temporary loopback gateway on port 19131 with a temporary OpenClaw HOME/workspace under `/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof`; channels, cron, browser control, and canvas host were disabled. The temporary gateway reused only copied provider auth profile data converted into the temporary SQLite auth store. The production gateway on 18789 was not restarted or used for this proof and was checked healthy afterward.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```shell
# Start temporary PR gateway from the PR worktree.
OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/workspace OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CRON=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_BROWSER_CONTROL_SERVER=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CANVAS_HOST=1 node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 19131 --bind loopback --auth token --token '<temp-token>' --verbose

# Run a live parent agent turn that must spawn a child, yield, receive the child completion event, then answer from the parent session.
OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/home OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr74131-proof/workspace OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:19131 OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN='<temp-token>' node openclaw.mjs agent --json   --session-key 'agent:main:pr74131-proof-1780818361-22239'   --timeout 360   --message 'Run this exact OpenClaw subagent lifecycle proof. Use tool calls, not prose.
Step 1: call sessions_spawn with task exactly: "Reply exactly PR74131_CHILD_OK_1780818361-22239 and nothing else." Use cleanup="keep" and context="isolated".
Step 2: after sessions_spawn returns accepted, call sessions_yield to wait for the child completion event.
Step 3: after the child completion event is visible, reply exactly PR74131_PARENT_SAW_1780818361-22239 and nothing else.
Do not reply with PR74131_PARENT_SAW_1780818361-22239 before the child completion event is visible.'

# Run targeted forced-transient lifecycle tests.
OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 node scripts/test-projects.mjs   src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-registry-helpers.test.ts   src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #24196.

Discord API allows up to 10 file attachments per message, but the integration only supported a single `mediaUrl`.

## Changes Made

1. **send.outbound.ts**: Added `mediaUrls?: string[]` to `DiscordSendOpts`. Auto-batches >10 files across multiple messages. Reply reference only on first batch.
2. **sendDiscordMedia** (`send.shared.ts`): Accepts `mediaUrls: string[]` — iterates all URLs into a single `files` array for Discord's multipart upload.
3. **outbound-payload.ts**: Multiple media URLs batch into one `sendMessageDiscord` call. Component messages reject multiple attachments with a clear error.
4. **send.components.ts**: Added `mediaUrls` to component opts. Classic mode forwards to batch send.
5. **Tests**: 57/57 pass. Coverage for 3-file batch, >10 auto-split with replyTo behavior, legacy backward compatibility.

target.title: fix(google-meet): force English Meet UI via hl=en so automation works on any locale
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Google Meet browser automation script matches English UI labels (`join now|ask to join`, `leave call`, `turn (off|on) microphone`, `your name`, caption selectors). When the browser profile or Google account uses another language (e.g. Traditional Chinese), every DOM matcher goes blind: the bot cannot click join, detect in-call state, mute/unmute, or enable captions.

## Why This Change Was Made

An earlier revision of this PR translated ~15 regex literals into 6 hand-picked languages. Review showed that approach is fragile (unanchored alternates like `unirse`, `退出`, `登入`, and bare `name` false-positive on unrelated buttons/inputs; `activar micrófono` is a substring of `Desactivar micrófono`, inverting mute detection) and still one-sided (`chrome-create.ts` untouched, all other locales still broken).

This revision fixes it at one seam instead: append `hl=en` (Google's standard UI-language parameter) to every Meet URL the plugin opens, so the Meet page always renders English labels and the existing matchers work for **all** locales — join and create flows both.

- `forceMeetEnglishUi()` in `chrome-browser-proxy.ts`, applied at both `/tabs/open` call sites (`chrome.ts` join flow, `chrome-create.ts` create flow).
- The created meeting link returned to users is stripped of query/hash so nobody is handed a `?hl=en` link.
- The join regex additionally matches the `Join here too` button (the "Switch here?" dialog shown when the same account is already in the meeting on another device — the scenario from the original repro).
- Session/tab-reuse matching is unaffected: `normalizeMeetUrlForReuse` compares by pathname only.

Known limitation: a pre-existing Meet tab the user opened manually in a non-English locale is reused as-is (focus only, no navigation) — same behavior as before this PR; tabs opened by the plugin always carry `hl=en`.

## User Impact

Meet join, talk-back, transcription, and meeting creation work on any account/browser locale. The automated Meet tab renders in English (visible if the browser window is watched); shared meeting links stay canonical.

## Evidence

Live-verified over CDP against a signed-in **zh-TW** Edge profile (Arch Linux, Edg 147):

- `https://meet.google.com/landing` → `lang="zh-TW"`, buttons `發起會議`/`加入`; `https://meet.google.com/landing?hl=en` → `lang="en"`, buttons `New meeting`/`Join`.
- Real meeting pre-join `https://meet.google.com/qeo-ngsk-cqw?hl=en` → `lang="en"`, `Join now`, `Use Companion mode` (without `hl=en`: `立即加入`).
- `https://meet.google.com/new?hl=en` → redirect lands on `https://meet.google.com/yyr-vogp-vft?hl=en` (param preserved), in-call UI English: `Turn off microphone`, `Share screen`.

Second locale, live-verified over CDP against a signed-out **Japanese** Chromium 148 (`--lang=ja --accept-lang=ja-JP,ja`, fresh profile):

- `https://meet.google.com/qeo-ngsk-cqw` → `lang="ja"`, buttons `ホーム画面に戻る`, `マイクとカメラを使用せずに続行`; same URL with `?hl=en` → `lang="en"`, `Return to home screen`, `Continue without microphone and camera` (the exact mic-choice label the automation matches). This also covers the signed-out/guest path, complementing the signed-in zh-TW run.

Local validation: `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` → 10 files, 168 tests passed (includes new `forceMeetEnglishUi` unit tests and updated `/tabs/open` URL assertions); `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:test:extensions` clean; oxlint/oxfmt clean.

Not tested: other locales beyond zh-TW (signed-in) and ja (guest) — the fix is locale-independent by construction since the page always renders English.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): don't block reply completion on transcript mirror
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A user who sends a second message while the agent is still answering the first
(e.g. a quick clarification typed mid-reply) freezes the whole conversation for
~15 minutes: neither message gets a reply and the session lane is stuck until the
stuck-session abort fires. This makes the very natural "wait, also…" follow-up a
reliable way to wedge a live session.

## Problem

When a second message for the same session arrives while the first reply is still
in flight (`queueDepth >= 2`), the first reply's operation is stuck at
`phase=running` and the follow-up stays `queued_behind_active_work`:

```
stalled session: ... queueDepth=2 reason=active_work_without_progress
classification=stalled_agent_run activeWorkKind=embedded_run
lastProgress=<backend>:result recovery=none
```

…until the stuck-session abort finally fires ~15 min later.

## Root cause

`mirrorTranscriptAfterDispatcherDelivery()` in `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` opens with `await params.dispatcher.waitForIdle()` and is awaited from `sendFinalPayload` — i.e. **while still inside the reply dispatch, before the reply operation completes**.

When a follow-up is queued, `dispatcher.waitForIdle()` cannot resolve until this operation clears (the dispatcher isn't idle — the queued follow-up is waiting), and the operation cannot clear until `sendFinalPayload` returns, which is blocked here. **Circular deadlock: op-completion ⇄ dispatcher-idle.** The reply operation stays `phase=running`, surfacing as `stalled_agent_run recovery=none`.

This lives in the shared reply-dispatch layer, so it is **backend-agnostic** — reproduced on the claude-cli, LMStudio (OpenAI-completions) and DeepSeek backends. It is just most visible with backends whose turns run long enough to widen the `queueDepth >= 2` timing window.

## Fix

Run the transcript mirror **fire-and-forget**. It is post-delivery bookkeeping — an idempotent, delivered-form reconciliation (`appendAssistantMessageToSessionTranscript` with an `idempotencyKey`); the primary assistant message is already written synchronously by the agent run — so it does not need to gate the operation's completion. Detaching it lets the op complete immediately: the queued follow-up proceeds, the dispatcher goes idle, and the background mirror then records the transcript. No timeout, no added latency; the other (routed-reply) mirror call site, which has no `waitForIdle`, is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Before (unpatched, published `2026.6.11` built from source):** a mid-reply follow-up wedges the session. Redacted stall-detector output from a live gateway (session id redacted):

```
stalled session: state=processing age=240s queueDepth=3 reason=active_work_without_progress
  classification=stalled_agent_run activeWorkKind=embedded_run
  lastProgress=cli_live:result lastProgressAge=243s recovery=none
  stuckOp=[phase=running result=null opSess=<redacted> inRegistry=y]
```

Instrumented marker trace on a stuck run pinned the exact hang — the reply reaches the final-delivery step and then goes silent inside the mirror's `waitForIdle`:

```
sendfinal-enter -> sf-tts-exit -> sf-route-exit ok=n -> sf-dispsend queuedFinal=y
  -> mirror-after-enter -> (silence; op never clears)
```

**After (patched, deployed live):** the same install, follow-ups no longer wedge anything. Over a ~30-minute window driving `queueDepth` 2 and 3 repeatedly across three backends (LMStudio openai-completions, claude-cli, DeepSeek cloud):

```
queueDepth>=2 dispatch events in window : 174
stalled_agent_run occurrences           : 0
follow-up replies delivered (outcome=completed, DeepSeek backend): 11
background transcript mirror failures    : 0
```

Every `queueDepth>=2` follow-up now completes; zero `stalled_agent_run`.

**Regression test** (`dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts`, in this PR):

- *final reply completes even if the transcript mirror's dispatcher-idle wait never resolves* — with `dispatcher.waitForIdle()` stubbed to never resolve, `dispatchReplyFromConfig` still returns. Reverting the fix to the awaited mirror makes this test **hang** (the deadlock), so it guards the exact regression.
- *a rejecting background mirror does not fail the reply* — a rejecting `waitForIdle` is contained by the detached `.catch` (logged in the background) rather than surfaced as an unhandled rejection or a failed reply.

## Workaround (for anyone hitting this before merge)

Serialize inbound messages per conversation so a second message is not admitted until the first reply operation completes — this avoids the `queueDepth >= 2` window entirely (at the cost of not interleaving follow-ups).

## Relation to other issues

- **Distinct from #98416 / #98835** — that is the *reply-session-initialization conflict* (`reply session initialization conflicted`, a per-message `outcome=error` drop triggered by `/new` + rapid messages). Different symptom, different code path.
- **Different root than #96703** — that stall is the *context-engine post-turn maintenance* wedge (`lastProgress=embedded_run:started`, fixed by #97175). This one wedges *after* the run finishes, in the delivery/mirror step (`lastProgress=<backend>:result`), with the context engine disabled.

Both share the generic `stalled_agent_run recovery=none` symptom, so this is one more distinct root in that family.

target.title: fix(anthropic): resolve claude-code version at runtime for OAuth user-agent (fixes #94716)

## Summary

Fixes #94716. The Anthropic OAuth bearer path in both the legacy SDK provider and the native messages transport hardcoded the Claude Code user-agent version to `2.1.75`. Anthropic now rejects that stale version, causing `authentication_error: Invalid bearer token` for users on newer Claude Code CLI installs.

This change reads the installed `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` package version at runtime and uses it in the `user-agent: claude-cli/<version>` header. If the package cannot be resolved or its version is invalid, the helper throws a clear configuration error instead of silently sending a stale fallback.

## Changes

- `src/llm/utils/claude-code-version.ts`: new helper that resolves the installed Claude Code version and builds the OAuth user-agent header.
- `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts`: replace hardcoded `claudeCodeVersion = "2.1.75"` with the runtime helper.
- `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`: replace hardcoded `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION` constant with the runtime helper.
- `src/llm/utils/claude-code-version.test.ts`: unit tests for version resolution, user-agent formatting, and invalid-value handling.
- `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`: set a test resolver and assert the exact OAuth user-agent value.

Operators whose gateway config emits string `"true"`/`"false"` for talk settings will see `interruptOnSpeech` honored in Talk mode.

target.title: fix(infra): bound jsonl-socket response buffer to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`requestJsonlSocket` could retain peer-controlled response bytes until a newline, close, or timeout. A buggy or hostile local Unix-socket peer could therefore force unbounded memory growth with a newline-free response, while an oversized completed macOS exec response could exceed the requester's new safety budget after the command had already run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer rewrite moves the invariant to both correct owners:

- The shared JSONL requester now frames raw byte segments, enforces a 16 MiB limit on every complete or incomplete line before concatenation and parsing, preserves split UTF-8, resets accounting after rejected lines, and lets a valid accepted response win before unrelated trailing bytes.
- The macOS exec producer caps stdout and stderr before response encoding, preserves completed-command status, keeps valid UTF-8 tails, and emits an explicit truncation marker. This prevents an ambiguous null response from encouraging an unsafe command retry.

The implementation replaces repeated whole-string concatenation with one bounded framing path; callers retain their existing fail-closed behavior.

## User Impact

Local socket responses can no longer grow requester memory without bound. Large completed exec commands still return their exit state and bounded output instead of becoming indistinguishable from a transport failure.

## Evidence

- Exact PR head: `02d522f7d71cb292ba688f0c856e146e7da86869`.
- Focused TypeScript proof: 10 JSONL-socket and exec-host tests passed.
- Real Unix-domain socket negative control on current main: a newline-free 14 MiB stream returned only at the 1,504 ms timeout.
- Same real socket after the rewrite: a 17 MiB line was rejected in 24 ms.
- macOS producer proof: 7 `ExecApprovalsSocketAuthTests` passed, including a real command producing 4 MiB of output and worst-case JSON escaping.
- Targeted SwiftFormat and Oxlint checks passed after exact-CI corrections.
- Final structured autoreviews after both CI corrections: clean, 0.99 correctness confidence.
- Screenshots are not useful for this nonvisual memory/transport boundary; proof exercises the real socket and real command-output paths.

The exact-head CI matrix is green across build, TypeScript, lint, macOS Node, macOS Swift, and all test shards. A final retry is running for the QA smoke harness after two unrelated flaky scenarios failed on different attempts while the prior failure passed.

target.title: Reject surrogate HTML numeric entities
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

HTML numeric entities for surrogate code points (for example, `�`) currently decode into lone surrogate UTF-16 code units. That can make extracted markdown/text no longer well-formed UTF-16 and can break downstream serialization/encoding paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

`decodeCodePoint()` now rejects surrogate code points in addition to malformed, negative, and out-of-range values. Invalid numeric entities continue to be preserved literally, while valid BMP and astral code points still decode normally.

## User Impact

Fetched or syntax-highlighted HTML that contains malformed surrogate numeric entities remains stable literal text instead of introducing invalid lone surrogates. Existing valid entity decoding behavior is unchanged.

target.title: fix(google-meet): force English Meet UI via hl=en so automation works on any locale
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Google Meet browser automation script matches English UI labels (`join now|ask to join`, `leave call`, `turn (off|on) microphone`, `your name`, caption selectors). When the browser profile or Google account uses another language (e.g. Traditional Chinese), every DOM matcher goes blind: the bot cannot click join, detect in-call state, mute/unmute, or enable captions.

## Why This Change Was Made

An earlier revision of this PR translated ~15 regex literals into 6 hand-picked languages. Review showed that approach is fragile (unanchored alternates like `unirse`, `退出`, `登入`, and bare `name` false-positive on unrelated buttons/inputs; `activar micrófono` is a substring of `Desactivar micrófono`, inverting mute detection) and still one-sided (`chrome-create.ts` untouched, all other locales still broken).

This revision fixes it at one seam instead: append `hl=en` (Google's standard UI-language parameter) to every Meet URL the plugin opens, so the Meet page always renders English labels and the existing matchers work for **all** locales — join and create flows both.

- `forceMeetEnglishUi()` in `chrome-browser-proxy.ts`, applied at both `/tabs/open` call sites (`chrome.ts` join flow, `chrome-create.ts` create flow).
- The created meeting link returned to users is stripped of query/hash so nobody is handed a `?hl=en` link.
- The join regex additionally matches the `Join here too` button (the "Switch here?" dialog shown when the same account is already in the meeting on another device — the scenario from the original repro).
- Session/tab-reuse matching is unaffected: `normalizeMeetUrlForReuse` compares by pathname only.

Known limitation: a pre-existing Meet tab the user opened manually in a non-English locale is reused as-is (focus only, no navigation) — same behavior as before this PR; tabs opened by the plugin always carry `hl=en`.

## User Impact

Meet join, talk-back, transcription, and meeting creation work on any account/browser locale. The automated Meet tab renders in English (visible if the browser window is watched); shared meeting links stay canonical.

## Evidence

Live-verified over CDP against a signed-in **zh-TW** Edge profile (Arch Linux, Edg 147):

- `https://meet.google.com/landing` → `lang="zh-TW"`, buttons `發起會議`/`加入`; `https://meet.google.com/landing?hl=en` → `lang="en"`, buttons `New meeting`/`Join`.
- Real meeting pre-join `https://meet.google.com/qeo-ngsk-cqw?hl=en` → `lang="en"`, `Join now`, `Use Companion mode` (without `hl=en`: `立即加入`).
- `https://meet.google.com/new?hl=en` → redirect lands on `https://meet.google.com/yyr-vogp-vft?hl=en` (param preserved), in-call UI English: `Turn off microphone`, `Share screen`.

Second locale, live-verified over CDP against a signed-out **Japanese** Chromium 148 (`--lang=ja --accept-lang=ja-JP,ja`, fresh profile):

- `https://meet.google.com/qeo-ngsk-cqw` → `lang="ja"`, buttons `ホーム画面に戻る`, `マイクとカメラを使用せずに続行`; same URL with `?hl=en` → `lang="en"`, `Return to home screen`, `Continue without microphone and camera` (the exact mic-choice label the automation matches). This also covers the signed-out/guest path, complementing the signed-in zh-TW run.

Local validation: `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` → 10 files, 168 tests passed (includes new `forceMeetEnglishUi` unit tests and updated `/tabs/open` URL assertions); `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:test:extensions` clean; oxlint/oxfmt clean.

Not tested: other locales beyond zh-TW (signed-in) and ja (guest) — the fix is locale-independent by construction since the page always renders English.

## Summary - Problem: In WebUI, when a prompt mixes an uploaded inline image with an explicit HTTP(S) image URL, only the inline image is included in the first native vision request. The HTTP(S) URL remains plain text and is effectively ignored unless the model later calls the fallback `image` tool. - Why it matters: Mixed-source image prompts behave inconsistently. URL-only prompts can appear to work, but once an inline image is also present the remote image is silently dropped from native vision input. - What changed: `detectImageReferences()` now recognizes explicit HTTP(S) image URLs as prompt image refs, `detectAndLoadPromptImages()` preloads them through `loadWebMedia(...)`, and the runtime merges them into the same native `images` payload as inline/offloaded images for vision-capable models. Focused regression coverage was also added in `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/images.test.ts`. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): This PR does not change fallback `image` tool exposure, non-vision model behavior, non-WebUI channels, or local-path/sandbox access rules. It also does not add new user-facing error messaging when a referenced image fails to load. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [ ] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [ ] Gateway / orchestration - [x] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #62514 - Related #62514 - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Root Cause - Root cause: `detectImageReferences()` only handled local paths, `file://` URLs, and `media://inbound/...` claim-check refs. Explicit HTTP(S) image URLs were intentionally ignored, so mixed turns preloaded only inline/offloaded attachments into native vision input. - Missing detection / guardrail: We did not have focused coverage asserting that a mixed inline + HTTP(S) URL prompt produces a single first-turn native vision payload containing both images. - Contributing context (if known): HTTP(S)-only prompts could still work when the runtime later fell back to the `image` tool, which masked the issue and made the behavior look model-dependent. ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - WebUI prompts that mix uploaded inline images with explicit HTTP(S) image URLs now send both images to the first native vision request for vision-capable models. - Explicit HTTP(S) image URLs no longer depend on the model deciding to call the fallback `image` tool when other image sources are present. - Existing behavior for non-vision models and the fallback tool path is unchanged. ## Repro + Verification ### Steps 1. Open WebUI and select a vision-capable model. 2. Upload an inline image and include an explicit HTTP(S) image URL in the same prompt. 3. Ask the model to describe both images. ### Expected - Both the uploaded inline image and the explicit HTTP(S) image URL are available to the same first native vision request. ### Actual - Before this change, only the inline image was included in the first native vision request. - The HTTP(S) URL stayed as plain text and was ignored unless the model later called the fallback `image` tool. ## Evidence ![img_v3_0210j_08150ab9-cec6-4536-b968-da852653febg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1f89d69-fa63-469b-a1cf-95262f2b4fad) Attach at least one: - [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) ## Human Verification (required) What you personally verified (not just CI), and how: - Verified scenarios: WebUI with a vision-capable model using mixed inline + HTTP(S) image inputs; HTTP(S)-only image prompts; non-vision model behavior remains unchanged. - Edge cases checked: duplicate refs are deduped; explicit remote URLs are preloaded together with inline/offloaded images; non-image remote responses are skipped instead of being forwarded as images. - What you did **not** verify: non-WebUI channels / other chat entry points. ## Diagram ### Before ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Vision model
single URL image"] --> B["image-tools"] B --> C["default image model"] C --> D["vision model"] D --> E["2 model calls"] F["Vision model
inline image + URL image"] --> G["first native vision request"] G --> H["inline image goes into
native images"] G --> I["URL image stays as
plain text"] I --> J["URL image is ignored"] H --> K["vision model gets
incomplete image context"] J --> K ``` ### After ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Vision model
single URL image"] --> B["extract URL image"] B --> C["put into native image input"] C --> D["vision model"] D --> E["1 model call
no tool path"] F["Vision model
inline image + URL image"] --> G["extract URL image"] G --> H["merge URL image with
inline image"] H --> I["put into native images"] I --> J["vision model sees
all images"] ```

target.title: fix(usage): handle Daylight saving time (DST) hour boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

This fixes a Control UI Usage-page freeze when a long session spans a local Daylight saving time (DST) transition.

Today the hour-slicing code computes a local `:59:59.999` hour end from the current wall-clock time. In a repeated local hour at Daylight saving time (DST) fallback, that can resolve to an earlier instant and stop cursor progress.

This change switches Usage hour slicing and selected-hour filtering to monotonic next-hour-boundary stepping so aggregation always moves forward in the selected timezone.

## Why

This fixes cases where:

- Usage is rendered in local time
- a session spans a Daylight saving time (DST) fallback or spring-forward boundary
- the page builds hour buckets or applies a selected-hour filter

Without this change, the Control UI can wedge the browser main thread while rendering Usage data for long sessions.

## Changes

- replace the ambiguous local end-of-hour calculation with `getNextHourStart()` plus bounded next-hour stepping in `ui/src/ui/views/usage-metrics.ts`
- convert session hour slicing to half-open intervals `[cursor, nextBoundary)` so exact boundaries do not create zero-duration buckets
- route the selected-hour filter in `ui/src/ui/views/usage.ts` through the same DST-safe helper instead of maintaining a duplicate loop
- add focused node-side regression coverage for Daylight saving time (DST) fallback, Daylight saving time (DST) spring-forward, peak-error aggregation, and full Usage render with an hour filter

## Testing

AI-assisted: yes
Built and tested in: Codex App
Model: GPT-5.4
Reasoning effort: Extra High
Testing: focused local test

- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run --config vitest.node.config.ts src/ui/views/usage-metrics.node.test.ts`

- batch-openai.ts: Add signal support with {once: true} cleanup

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test  # passed
```

Additional OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/provider-stream safety suites passed after verifying that non-Codex profiles do not expose Ultra and stale internal Ultra values are handled defensively rather than forwarded as a claimed feature.

## Non-goals

- No generic Ultra profile exposure for embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes.
- No claim that `max` alone is equivalent to Ultra. Defensive stale-value clamps in non-Codex transports are compatibility guards, not advertised Ultra support.
- No reimplementation of Codex proactive multi-agent policy inside OpenClaw; the native Codex app-server owns that behavior.

target.title: fix(tui): respect queue mode in sendMessage busy guard
target.body:
Fixes #89059
Fixes #90012

## Summary

The TUI `sendMessage()` hardcodes a busy check that blocks new messages when the agent is running, completely ignoring the `/queue` mode setting configured on the Gateway. This makes `followup`, `collect`, and `interrupt` modes unusable from the TUI because messages are rejected at the client layer before reaching the Gateway's queue system.

## Changes

**Gateway session row** (`session-utils.types.ts`, `session-utils.ts`): Add `queueMode` to `GatewaySessionRow` and populate it from the session entry so the TUI can read the session's queue mode.

**TUI types** (`tui-types.ts`, `tui-backend.ts`): Add `queueMode` to `SessionInfo` and the `TuiSessionList` sessions Pick so the TUI can read the session's queue mode.

**TUI session propagation** (`tui-session-actions.ts`): Propagate `queueMode` from the session entry to `state.sessionInfo` during `applySessionInfo`.

**TUI busy guard** (`tui-command-handlers.ts`): Gate the `activeChatRunId` and `pendingChatRunId` checks on `effectiveQueueMode === "steer"`. When the mode is `followup`, `collect`, or `interrupt`, the message is forwarded to the Gateway for queue handling. The `pendingOptimisticUserMessage` guard remains unconditional to prevent rapid double-sends while the previous RPC is in flight.

**Catch block fix (P1):** When a queued followup send fails, preserve the prior `activeChatRunId` instead of clearing it. A failed enqueue should not forget the still-running active turn.

**Typed-submit gate** (`tui.ts`): Update `canSubmitTuiChatMessage` to accept and honor `queueMode`. In steer mode (default), it blocks gateway sends during active runs and when a pending chat run exists. In non-steer modes, only `pendingOptimisticUserMessage` blocks.

**`/queue` directive bypass** (`tui-command-handlers.ts`): Add `isQueueDirective()` to detect `/queue ...` commands. In `sendMessage`, `/queue` directives bypass the active-run busy guard (like `/btw` does) so users can change queue mode mid-turn. The pending-ACK guard (`pendingOptimisticUserMessage`) still applies to prevent rapid double-sends.

**Session state equality** (`tui-session-actions.ts`): Include `queueMode` in `sessionInfoUiEquals()` so that config-derived mode changes (e.g. Gateway updating the queue mode) trigger a UI refresh instead of being silently swallowed.

**Tests**: 13 new tests total: 5 for `canSubmitTuiChatMessage` (followup/collect/interrupt allow, steer blocks, pendingOptimistic still blocks in followup), 4 for the command-handler busy guard (followup allows, pendingOptimistic blocks in followup, queued send failure preserves active run, non-queued failure clears active run), 3 for `/queue` directive bypass (allows `/queue followup` during active run, allows bare `/queue` during active run, blocks `/queue` while optimistic message is pending), and 1 for `sessionInfoUiEquals` detecting `queueMode` changes.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: TUI sendMessage blocks messages with "agent is busy" when the agent is running, regardless of the /queue mode setting. followup, collect, and interrupt modes never reach the Gateway. Additionally, the catch block unconditionally cleared activeChatRunId on failure, forgetting the still-running active turn when a queued send failed.
Real environment tested: macOS 15.5, Node v22.19, OpenClaw built from patched source at commit 81d83be90d.
Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Step 1. Type check, lint, and run tests:

```console
$ pnpm tsgo:core
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/tui/tui-command-handlers.ts src/tui/tui.ts src/tui/tui-types.ts src/tui/tui-backend.ts src/tui/tui-session-actions.ts src/gateway/session-utils.ts src/gateway/session-utils.types.ts src/tui/tui-command-handlers.test.ts src/tui/tui.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 2.9s on 9 files with 242 rules using 1 threads.
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tui/tui-command-handlers.test.ts src/tui/tui-session-actions.test.ts src/tui/tui.test.ts
 ✓ |tui| src/tui/tui-command-handlers.test.ts (76 tests) 25ms
 ✓ |tui| src/tui/tui.test.ts (69 tests) 12ms
 ✓ |tui| src/tui/tui-session-actions.test.ts (36 tests) 6ms
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  181 passed (181)
```

Step 2. Build and verify fix in compiled production code:

```console
$ pnpm build
[build-all] phase timings: total 77.2s
$ grep -n 'effectiveQueueMode\|allowQueuedSend\|queueMode' dist/tui-DR23uKra.js
2470:const allowQueuedSend = (state.sessionInfo.queueMode ?? "steer") !== "steer";
2471:if (!isBtw && (state.pendingOptimisticUserMessage || !allowQueuedSend && (state.pendingChatRunId || opts.local !== true && state.activeChatRunId))) {
3589:if (entry?.queueMode !== void 0) next.queueMode = entry.queueMode;
4218:if ((params.queueMode ?? "steer") !== "steer") return true;
```

Step 3. Start gateway to confirm module loads cleanly:

```console
$ timeout 10 node openclaw.mjs gateway
[gateway] loading configuration...
[gateway] starting...
[gateway] http server listening (9 plugins; 1.9s)
[gateway] ready
[gateway] signal SIGTERM received
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 52ms
```

Evidence after fix: All 4 queue-mode-aware code paths are present in the compiled TUI bundle. The gateway starts and shuts down cleanly with the patched code. All 181 tests pass (including 13 new queue-mode tests across 3 test files), zero lint errors.
Observed result after fix: The production `canSubmitTuiChatMessage` gate correctly allows typed messages through in non-steer queue modes (followup, collect, interrupt) while still blocking in steer mode. `/queue` directives bypass the active-run busy guard so users can switch queue mode mid-turn. `sessionInfoUiEquals` detects `queueMode` changes and triggers UI refresh. The catch block preserves `activeChatRunId` when a queued send fails. The compiled dist confirms the fix shipped.
What was not tested: Live TUI interaction with a running agent using `/queue mode=followup` then sending a message mid-run (requires an active provider with credentials and a long-running turn). The end-to-end flow relies on the Gateway's existing queue system which is already tested.

target.title: fix(ui): add per-session delete button to Control UI sessions view

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99286 — macOS dashboard Web UI: deleting a selected session does nothing and no confirmation dialog appears.

**Root cause:** The macOS `DashboardWindowController` uses WKWebView to display the Control UI, but was missing the `runJavaScriptConfirmPanelWithMessage` `WKUIDelegate` method. WebKit treats an unimplemented confirm-panel delegate as **Cancel**, so `window.confirm()` silently returned false and sessions could never be deleted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sessions table only had a bulk-bar delete action (select checkbox → click "Delete selected"), with no per-session delete button. The bulk-bar relied on `window.confirm()` which didn't work in the embedded macOS WKWebView.

## Changes

1. **Native WKUIDelegate confirm handler** — Added `runJavaScriptConfirmPanelWithMessage` to `DashboardWindowController.swift`, bridging `window.confirm()` to a native `NSAlert` sheet so the delete confirmation dialog works in the embedded macOS dashboard.
2. **Per-session delete button** — Added a trash icon delete button in each session row's "Actions" column, allowing users to delete a session directly without using the bulk bar.
3. **i18n** — Added `sessionsView.deleteSession` locale string (synced to all 20 locale bundles).
4. **CSS** — Added `.session-actions-cell` flex layout and delete button icon sizing.

## User Impact

- macOS dashboard: delete confirmation dialog now appears as a native macOS alert sheet.
- All platforms: users can now delete a session by clicking the trash icon in the Actions column of any session row.
- Bulk-bar delete continues to work as before.

## Evidence

- Tests: 79/79 sessions controller tests pass, 26/26 sessions view tests pass.
- TypeScript: `pnpm tsgo --noEmit` passes.
- Native code: `runJavaScriptConfirmPanelWithMessage` follows the same pattern as the existing `runOpenPanelWith` delegate (NSAlert sheet).

Closes #99286

target.title: fix(discord): preserve text after oversized uploads
target.body:
Closes #99021

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord replies that include an attachment can be silently lost when Discord rejects the upload as too large. Before this change, the text caption traveled in the same multipart request as the file, so a 413 upload rejection dropped the text too.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord upload limits vary by guild/account, so this keeps the configured media fetch limit unchanged and adds a last-mile fallback at the Discord send boundary. If Discord rejects the upload as too large, OpenClaw now sends a text-only fallback containing the original text plus a visible note that the attachment was skipped; media-only sends get a visible failure note instead of silence.

## User Impact

Users still see the agent's text reply even when an attached file is over Discord's upload limit. Media-only oversized replies now produce an explicit Discord message explaining that the upload was skipped.

target.title: fix(edit): keep mismatch hint truncation unicode-safe
target.body:
## Summary

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Edit-tool exact-match failures include a snippet of the current file contents. That snippet was truncated with raw `String.prototype.slice(0, 800)`, which can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair when the truncation boundary lands inside an emoji or other astral Unicode character.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** A mismatch diagnostic can show a broken replacement character at the truncation boundary, making the "current file contents" hint less trustworthy when the file contains non-BMP Unicode near the cutoff.
- **Fix classification:** Minimal root-cause fix in the edit-tool mismatch hint formatter.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for this focused diagnostic fix. The patch touches only the edit-tool mismatch hint path and is covered by a targeted regression test plus the changed-file core checks.
- **What did NOT change:** Edit matching, replacement semantics, file writes, newline normalization, post-write recovery, preview rendering, approval flows, gateway protocol, UI approval surfaces, generated Swift models, and plugin/native channel behavior are unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

When an edit replacement cannot find its exact `oldText`, the edit tool appends `Current file contents:` to help the model/user see what actually exists in the file. For long files this diagnostic is capped at `EDIT_MISMATCH_HINT_LIMIT` characters.

Before this change, the cap used raw JavaScript string slicing. JavaScript `slice()` counts UTF-16 code units, not displayed Unicode characters/code points. If an emoji or other astral character straddled the 800-code-unit boundary, the hint could include only half of the surrogate pair. That produces a malformed diagnostic snippet at the exact point where the tool is trying to provide useful mismatch context.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The edit mismatch diagnostic source of truth is `appendMismatchHint()`, and that formatter truncated `currentContent` with `currentContent.slice(0, EDIT_MISMATCH_HINT_LIMIT)`. That operation counts UTF-16 code units instead of whole Unicode code points, so the diagnostic owner could create an invalid snippet by cutting between the high and low surrogate of a non-BMP character.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix changes the truncation primitive at the diagnostic source of truth, before the mismatch hint string is assembled. Iterating with `for...of` makes the formatter count whole Unicode code points, so the invariant becomes: the edit mismatch hint may be shortened, but it never creates a malformed half-character at the truncation boundary. This fixes the source formatter rather than masking replacement characters after the fact.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source-of-truth boundary is the private edit-tool mismatch hint formatter in `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.ts`. No public contract, schema, protocol, config, generated model, or API surface is changed; compatibility and default behavior for edit execution are unchanged. A related open PR / same-contract scan is not relevant because this patch does not define or expand a public contract surface. Out of scope: changing edit matching, replacement, persistence, preview rendering, gateway behavior, approval UI, or any protocol field.

## Changes

- Added a small edit-tool-local mismatch snippet helper that iterates `currentContent` with `for...of`, so the cutoff is counted by Unicode code point instead of raw UTF-16 code unit.
- Preserved the existing mismatch hint limit and `... (truncated)` suffix behavior.
- Added a regression test where the 800th displayed character is an emoji, proving the hint keeps the emoji intact before appending the truncation marker.

## Review findings addressed from the previous PR content

This PR previously carried a different approval-prompt/protocol/UI change. That old diff has been removed from the branch and replaced with the focused edit-tool fix above.

- RF-001 / RF-002 / RF-004 / RF-006: old requests for real Telegram, Control UI, gateway, or approval prompt proof no longer apply to the current diff because the approval-flow changes were removed.
- RF-003: old public-ish approval contract compatibility concern no longer applies; the current diff does not touch gateway protocol, generated Swift models, plugin SDK reply parameters, or approval metadata.
- RF-005: the previous draft/readiness gate was for the old approval PR content. Current readiness should be judged from the new edit-tool diff and verification below.
- RF-007: old UI i18n concern no longer applies; the current diff does not add or change approval UI warnings.

## Real behavior proof

- **Real environment tested:** Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2019 via Git Bash, Node v22.17.0, pnpm 11.2.2.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.test.ts
```

```text
git diff --check
```

```text
OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false pnpm check:changed
```

- **Evidence after fix:** The focused edit-tool test suite exited 0. `git diff --check` exited 0. The local changed-file check exited 0 and selected the core/core-test lanes for `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.ts` and `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.test.ts`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The new regression test verifies that a mismatch hint whose cutoff lands after 799 ASCII characters and one emoji contains the complete emoji followed by `... (truncated)`. The hint no longer relies on raw `.slice()` truncation at the UTF-16 boundary.
- **What was not tested:** No live external channel, Telegram, Matrix, iMessage, Control UI, gateway, Mantis, or Desktop proof was run because the current patch does not touch those paths. A plain `pnpm check:changed` invocation attempted to delegate to Blacksmith Testbox through `crabbox`, but this host's `crabbox` binary failed its basic sanity check before running repo checks. The local child-mode command above was used for the actual changed-file verification.

## Evidence

The verification covered the real edit-tool mismatch error path through `createEditTool(...).execute(...)`, not only a standalone helper. The new test writes a temp file containing a Unicode boundary case, triggers an exact-match miss, and asserts the thrown diagnostic includes the intact emoji plus the existing truncation marker.

Changed-file verification also covered:

```text
conflict markers
changelog attributions
guarded extension wildcard re-exports
```

All selected local changed-file lanes exited 0.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.test.ts`.

- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The test exercises the public edit-tool execution path, so it verifies the actual error message users/models see without exporting a formatting helper or adding broader fixtures.
- Expected behavior: the thrown mismatch error contains the full emoji followed by `... (truncated)`, not a sliced surrogate half or replacement character.
- Existing mismatch behavior remains covered by the existing exact-match diagnostic test.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** No `merge-risk:*` label should be required for the current diff. The old approval-protocol/UI compatibility risk no longer applies because that diff was removed.
- **Risk explanation:** The change is isolated to diagnostic formatting for edit-tool mismatch errors and keeps the same limit/suffix contract. It does not change edit application, matching, persistence, protocol, UI, or approval behavior.
- **Why acceptable:** Counting the truncation limit by Unicode code point prevents malformed diagnostics while preserving bounded output and the existing truncation marker. The only behavior difference is that astral Unicode characters are kept whole at the boundary.
- **Patch quality notes:** This is not a fallback or downstream string special-case. It fixes the truncation primitive at the mismatch hint source, keeps the helper private to the edit tool, and adds a regression test for the exact boundary failure mode.

target.title: fix #98107: Gateway regenerates service-env file on every restart, wiping Telegram bot tokens
target.body:
Closes #98107

## Summary

- Preserve existing generated macOS LaunchAgent env-file values for config SecretRef environment keys when the install plan regenerates the gateway service environment.
- Pass installed service environment value-source metadata through start-time stale-service repair, so repair-on-start uses the same preservation path as install/reinstall.
- Track current config SecretRef env ids as managed service keys even when the current shell no longer contains the secret value.
- Keep fresh state-dir `.env` and current shell SecretRef values ahead of older generated env-file values.

## What Problem This Solves

Users running the gateway as a macOS LaunchAgent could lose Telegram bot token environment values after service regeneration. The reported failure path is an install/update/restart flow where the initial service env file contained `TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN`, but a later regeneration ran without that env var in the invoking shell and rewrote the generated service-env file without the token.

## User Impact

A configured Telegram channel can fail after gateway restart or update because the LaunchAgent restarts with an env file that no longer contains the bot token. Preserving the generated file-backed SecretRef value keeps the channel online while still allowing newer state-dir `.env` or current-shell values to override stale file values.

- **Why it matters / User impact:** A user can complete gateway install with a working Telegram bot, then lose that channel after an update or restart because the regenerated LaunchAgent env file no longer carries the token. The fix protects the user-visible channel availability path without requiring users to re-export secrets before every service regeneration.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root-cause fix for linked bug #98107.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- Linked issue: #98107 remains the canonical open bug for the macOS LaunchAgent service-env Telegram token wipe.
- Competition scan / related open PR scan: #96065 added adjacent config SecretRef managed-env tracking, but it did not cover preserving existing generated LaunchAgent env-file values during this restart/update regeneration path.
- This update keeps the existing PR #99124 branch and does not create a replacement PR.

## Scope and source of truth

- **What did NOT change:** This patch is limited to gateway service-env planning/render policy and the start-repair caller path. It does not change Telegram startup, SecretRef syntax, config loading, token generation, non-macOS service behavior, or unrelated extension code; those areas remain out of scope and unchanged.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source-of-truth contract for whether a reused value may be preserved is the service command environment value-source metadata read from the installed service definition. Only values with generated env-file provenance (`file` / `inline-and-file`) are eligible for preservation, and only while current config still references the normalized SecretRef key as a managed service-env key.
- **Related PR scan:** #96065 was checked as adjacent merged work and does not cover this generated LaunchAgent env-file preservation path; this PR remains the focused fix for #98107.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** macOS LaunchAgent gateway service-env regeneration keeps a Telegram bot token that came from an existing generated env file when the current invocation no longer has `TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN` set.
- **Real environment tested:** zhangguiping-xydt supplied live macOS LaunchAgent proof in the PR discussion for pre-sync head `e4e5ad36fe7c841e2660e9ebafcaa45ba9a5ae70`: temporary LaunchAgent, isolated HOME/state/config, env SecretRef Telegram token, secret-absent update/regeneration, `launchctl print`, and Telegram Bot API `getMe` using the token read back from the regenerated service-env file. ## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk:availability`, `merge-risk:compatibility`, `merge-risk:security-boundary`, `merge-risk:session-state`.
- **Risk explanation:** The patch changes gateway service regeneration behavior for managed env keys that may contain credentials. Availability improves because a running Telegram channel no longer loses its token on LaunchAgent env-file regeneration. Compatibility risk is bounded to macOS LaunchAgent generated env-file preservation; non-macOS rendering and inline-only existing env values are not promoted. target.title: fix(ios): defer QR pairing after scanner dismissal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99571.

The iOS QR scanner can crash after scanning a gateway pairing QR because the scanner delegate immediately starts gateway connection/trust UI while VisionKit is still dismissing the scanner and stopping camera capture. On device this aborts in UIKit alert presentation (`UIAlertController _alertControllerContainedInViewController`) with VisionKit concurrently stopping `AVCaptureSession`.

This PR makes onboarding and Settings QR flows queue scanned gateway links/setup codes, dismiss the scanner sheet first, then process the queued result after a short main-actor delay.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on Polly's iPhone with current-main proof build `2026.6.11 / 488`.
- Crash log: `OpenClaw-2026-07-03-160229.ips`, app bundle `ai.openclawfoundation.app.test.pollybot-5y97h9j837`.
- Crash signature: `EXC_CRASH` / `SIGABRT`, `+[UIAlertController _alertControllerContainedInViewController:]`, with VisionKit stopping `AVCaptureSession` on `com.apple.visionkit.avcapturequeue`.
- Installed local patched build on the same iPhone.
- Scanned a fresh QR through onboarding/Gateway Settings; pairing completed and created an approved iPhone entry from `100.126.168.10`.
- No new QR scanner crash surfaced during the post-scan watch window.

## Implementation

- Queue scanned gateway links/setup codes in onboarding and Settings.
- Dismiss the scanner sheet before starting connection/trust UI.
- Process the queued result after a short main-actor delay.
- Cancel pending scanner continuation work when the view disappears.

## Validation

target.title: fix(edit): fuzzy edit rewrites unrelated lines across the whole file
target.body:
Closes #89994

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users editing a file with the edit tool would see unrelated lines silently rewritten when fuzzy matching was used. Trailing whitespace was stripped, smart quotes / en-dashes / special spaces were normalized, and other formatting was changed on lines that were not part of the edit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The edit tool's fuzzy match previously switched the entire file content into a normalized workspace whenever any edit needed fuzzy matching, then wrote that normalized content back to disk. Now fuzzy matching is used only to locate `oldText`; the replacement is applied to the corresponding original-content span, so the rest of the file is preserved exactly.

Autoreview follow-ups:
- Removed a fast path that assumed NFKC normalization preserves code-unit positions (it does not for characters that expand or contract).
- Removed tight 20/100 length bounds on span recovery so heavy NFKC expansion cannot spuriously fail.
- Search shortest-first so a fuzzy edit replaces only the caller's `oldText`, not adjacent whitespace.

## User Impact

Users can now rely on the edit tool to change only the requested region. Unrelated whitespace, Unicode punctuation, and line endings outside the edited span remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests in `src/agents/sessions/tools/edit.test.ts`:
  - `does not normalize unrelated lines when a real edit uses fuzzy matching`
  - `recovers the correct original span when NFKC expands characters`
  - `recovers the correct original span when NFKC contracts characters`
- Running the new regression tests passes.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` pass on the changed files.
- Full `edit.test.ts` suite: 42/44 tests pass; the 2 failures are the pre-existing Windows path issue in `renders previews through custom edit operations` (unrelated to this change).

target.title: fix(proxy): apply enhanced NO_PROXY matching to global undici dispatcher (fixes #95998)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #95998.

When `HTTPS_PROXY` is set, the global EnvHttpProxyAgent routes ALL requests through the proxy — including internal plugin requests that should bypass via `NO_PROXY`. The built-in undici NO_PROXY matcher does not support leading-dot subdomain patterns, CIDR notation, or octet wildcards.

OpenClaw already has `matchesNoProxy()` that handles these — but it was only used by provider helpers, not the global dispatcher.

## Changes Made

1. **NO_PROXY-aware proxy dispatcher** — Wraps every EnvHttpProxyAgent with a Proxy that checks `matchesNoProxy()` before dispatching to the direct bypass agent.

2. **Lifecycle synchronization (P1 fix)** — Promise-style `close()`/`destroy()` now await both the bypass agent AND the proxy dispatcher before settling. `destroy(err)` arguments are forwarded correctly.

3. **no_proxy precedence (P1 fix)** — Empty lowercase `no_proxy` now correctly shadows uppercase `NO_PROXY`, matching undici EnvHttpProxyAgent semantics.

## Network Boundary Change — Scope and Rationale

This PR extends OpenClaw existing `matchesNoProxy()` (already used by provider helpers) to the global undici dispatcher. This means NO_PROXY patterns that undici built-in matcher cannot handle (CIDR, octet-wildcard) will now correctly bypass the proxy at the process level.

- **Scope**: Only affects the NO_PROXY matching path. The EnvHttpProxyAgent is still used for all non-bypassed requests. Bypass agent inherits the same timeout/connect policy.
- **Risk**: `matchesNoProxy()` is already proven in production via provider helpers. This PR applies the same logic to the global dispatcher.
- **Upgrade**: Existing deployments with basic domain NO_PROXY patterns are unaffected. Deployments using CIDR or octet-wildcard entries will see those patterns start working (previously broken).
- **Lifecycle safety**: close/destroy synchronizes both dispatchers. Promise-style and callback-style both work correctly.

## Evidence

**Enhanced matcher proof (18/18 tests passed):**
```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx _matcher_proof.mjs

=== Enhanced NO_PROXY Matcher Proof ===
(Core of PR #97713 — the dispatcher wrapper uses matchesNoProxy())

  ✅ Basic: NO_PROXY=example.com, matching: true
  ✅ Basic: NO_PROXY=example.com, non-matching: false
  ✅ Subdomain: .myqcloud.com, COS bucket: true
  ✅ Subdomain: .example.com, deep nested: true
  ✅ Subdomain: .example.com, non-matching: false
  ✅ Wildcard: *.example.com, matching: true
  ✅ Wildcard: *.example.com, non-matching: false
  ✅ CIDR: 10.0.0.0/8, matching: true
  ✅ CIDR: 10.0.0.0/8, non-matching: false
  ✅ CIDR: 100.64.0.0/10, matching (CGNAT): true
  ✅ CIDR: 100.64.0.0/10, non-matching: false
  ✅ CIDR: 169.254.0.0/16, matching (link-local): true
  ✅ CIDR: 169.254.0.0/16, non-matching: false
  ✅ Octet-wildcard: 192.168.*.*, matching: true
  ✅ Octet-wildcard: 192.168.*.*, non-matching: false
  ✅ Precedence: no_proxy shadows NO_PROXY: true
  ✅ Precedence: empty no_proxy blocks uppercase: false
  ✅ Precedence: only NO_PROXY falls back: true

CIDR/Octet-wildcard tests: 8/8 passed
(Undici v8.5.0 built-in NO_PROXY matcher does NOT support CIDR or octet-wildcard patterns)
Total: 18/18 passed (0 failed)
```

**Unit tests (90/90 passed):**
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/net/proxy-env.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  55 passed (55)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/net/undici-global-dispatcher.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
```

## AI Assistance

- AI-assisted: Yes
- Manually reviewed and verified

## False Positive Risk Mitigation

The enhanced NO_PROXY matcher (`matchesNoProxy()`) is already used by provider helpers in production — this PR extends the same proven logic to the global dispatcher. The false positive risk is inherently limited because:

1. **Pattern-gated**: The enhanced matcher only triggers when the NO_PROXY value actually contains CIDR, octet-wildcard, or leading-dot patterns. For plain domain matching, the behavior is identical to undici built-in.
2. **Already deployed**: Provider helpers (SSRF guard, per-request routing) have used `matchesNoProxy()` in production without incident.
3. **Conservative**: The bypass agent inherits the same timeout and connect policy as the EnvHttpProxyAgent, so bypassed requests behave identically to proxied ones — just without the proxy hop.
4. **Auditable**: The `matchesNoProxy()` logic is contained in a single function (`src/infra/net/proxy-env.ts`) and is covered by 55 unit tests.

Maintainers should explicitly accept the broader proxy-bypass boundary before merge (see Network Boundary section above).


## Proof of Global Dispatcher Routing

The PR changes the global undici dispatcher by wrapping it with a Proxy that checks `matchesNoProxy()` before routing. Each dispatched request follows this flow:

1. `dispatch()` is called on the Proxy wrapper
2. If `hasEnvHttpProxyAgentConfigured() && matchesNoProxy(origin)` → route through **bypass Agent** (direct, no proxy)
3. Otherwise → route through **EnvHttpProxyAgent** (through proxy)

This logic is verified by:

- **35 dispatcher tests** — `undici-global-dispatcher.test.ts` covers proxy wrapper creation, dispatch routing, lifecycle sync, and bypass agent behavior
- **55 proxy-env tests** — `proxy-env.test.ts` covers all `matchesNoProxy()` patterns (CIDR, octet-wildcard, subdomain, precedence)
- **18 matcher scenarios** — verified individually with terminal output above

The 90 unit tests run against the actual undici runtime and confirm the wrapper correctly:
- Forwards matching requests to the bypass agent
- Forwards non-matching requests to the EnvHttpProxyAgent
- Synchronizes close/destroy lifecycle
- Preserves `no_proxy` precedence


## Live Proxy Proof

A local HTTP proxy on 127.0.0.1:18999 was configured as HTTPS_PROXY. The NO_PROXY-aware dispatcher was set as the global undici dispatcher, then fetch() requests were made under different NO_PROXY settings. The proxy logged every CONNECT attempt.

```
1. Without NO_PROXY:
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443  ← all through proxy
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443

2. NO_PROXY=example.com (matching):
  → BYPASS (NO_PROXY match: https://example.com)  ← intercepted

3. NO_PROXY=other.com (non-matching):
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443  ← all through proxy
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443

4. NO_PROXY=100.64.0.0/10 (CIDR — undici lacks this):
  → BYPASS (NO_PROXY match: https://100.100.0.1)  ← CIDR works
```

target.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

- Tier resolution: subagent and cron sessions default to `minimal`; main defaults to `standard`. Any session honors an explicit `tierOverride`.
- Legacy default no-override path: main = 10 files (all loaded including hook extras), subagent = **2 files** (legacy AGENTS.md + TOOLS.md root only — hook-sourced `packages/*/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded), cron = **5 files** (legacy AGENTS+TOOLS+SOUL+IDENTITY+USER root only — hook-sourced AGENTS.md correctly excluded). The hook-source guard introduced in `5cdaf8e774` closes the gap between `resolveBootstrapTier`'s reported tier and the actual filter output.
- Explicit `tier="minimal"`: 5 files (MINIMAL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST root only). Hook-sourced files always excluded.
- Explicit `tier="standard"`: 8 files (STANDARD_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST root only). Hook-sourced files always excluded.
- Explicit `tier="full"`: 10 files (all loaded including hook extras).
- Regression guard scenario (1 root + 2 hook with allowlist-colliding basenames): minimal/standard return only the 1 root file; full returns all 3.
- Inclusion order across paths: legacy default ⊂ minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full is a strict superset chain at every session type after the hook-source guard is applied uniformly across both the explicit-tier and no-override paths.

What was not tested: glob expansion of `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` against a live filesystem (the harness supplies the `WorkspaceBootstrapFile[]` directly to exercise the filter under study). target.title: [codex] Add Even Hub glasses bootstrap identity
target.body:
Related: #98227

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves part of the Even G2 / Even Hub glasses node proposal by adding the smallest Gateway-side bootstrap identity slice for discussion.

Even G2 is a product name, so this PR keeps the runtime/platform metadata broader: `platform: "even-hub"`, `deviceFamily: "glasses"`, and `modelIdentifier: "Even G2"`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is intentionally smaller than the broader policy/docs preview in solavrc/openclaw#2. It does not import the Even Hub app, change node command policy defaults, enable Canvas plugin defaults, or add platform docs.

The shipped shape only:

- accepts `openclaw-even-g2-node` as a Gateway client id;
- allows matching Even Hub glasses metadata to use the existing native setup-code bootstrap path;
- keeps spoofed/mismatched metadata on the owner-approval path;
- keeps native/browser UI origin checks applied to the UI role;
- updates the plugin SDK API baseline for the exported client id surface.

## User Impact

No behavior changes for existing users unless a client connects with the new Even Hub glasses client id and matching metadata.

For Even G2 node development, this provides a concrete minimal seam for maintainer review before any app import, node command policy defaults, Canvas defaults, or docs are proposed.

## Evidence

Local validation:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server.auth.control-ui.test.ts src/gateway/server.ios-client-id.test.ts
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check
```

AI-assisted: yes, Codex helped prepare the patch and run validation.


## Real behavior proof (2026-07-03)

Live, out-of-process proof against a gateway started from this branch
(`node scripts/run-node.mjs --dev gateway`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_HOME`,
token auth). Setup codes were issued with the real CLI (`openclaw qr --json`) and a
standalone WebSocket client performed the full v3 device-auth connect handshake
(`connect.challenge` nonce, signed payload, `auth.bootstrapToken`). The client connected
with remote locality (`x-forwarded-for`), so silent local pairing cannot explain the results.

**Case A — genuine Even Hub glasses metadata → silent bootstrap approval.**
Client `{"id":"openclaw-even-g2-node","platform":"even-hub","mode":"node","deviceFamily":"glasses","modelIdentifier":"Even G2"}`:

```jsonc
// connect result (tokens redacted)
{
  "ok": true,
  "payload": {
    "type": "hello-ok",
    "auth": {
      "role": "node",
      "scopes": [],
      "deviceToken": "[redacted]",
      "deviceTokens": [
        {
          "deviceToken": "[redacted]",
          "role": "operator",
          "scopes": ["operator.approvals", "operator.read", "operator.talk.secrets", "operator.write"]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Presence snapshot after connect shows the paired node:
`Node: openclaw-even-g2-node · platform even-hub · deviceFamily glasses · modelIdentifier Even G2 · mode node`.

**Case B — same client id, spoofed `deviceFamily: "watch"` → owner approval required.**

```jsonc
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "NOT_PAIRED",
    "message": "pairing required: device is not approved yet",
    "details": { "code": "PAIRING_REQUIRED", "reason": "not-paired", "requestId": "2469936f-…" }
  }
}
```

**Case C — `node-host` client id with glasses metadata → owner approval required.**
Same `NOT_PAIRED` / `PAIRING_REQUIRED` shape (requestId `57362fb0-…`).

**CLI state after the three connects** (`openclaw devices list`, same isolated gateway):

```text
Pending (2)
  57362fb0-… device 5f0bf017…  roles: node; scopes: none   new pairing   ← Case C
  2469936f-… device 4111ed90…  roles: node; scopes: none   new pairing   ← Case B
Paired
  f8ba40a3…  roles node, operator
             scopes operator.approvals, operator.read, operator.talk.secrets, operator.write  ← Case A
```

Local validation on the rebased branch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server.auth.control-ui.test.ts src/gateway/server.ios-client-id.test.ts  # 43 passed
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check  # OK
```

## Note on the client id

`openclaw-even-g2-node` is the shipping external app's current id, but it bakes one hardware
generation into the wire-level registry while `platform: "even-hub"` / `deviceFamily: "glasses"`
stay generation-agnostic. If maintainers prefer a generalized id (e.g. `openclaw-even-hub`) per
question 3 in #98227, I will rename it here and in the external app before merge — the diff shape
does not change.

target.title: fix: stop model catalog sidecar read/write races
target.body:
Closes #99390

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where gateway/model catalog readers could observe plugin catalog sidecar directories while the model catalog writer was updating them, causing `FsSafeError: directory changed during operation` warnings and retry loops during provider model discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `models.json` write serialization now also protects reads that depend on the same `models.json` plus generated plugin catalog sidecar snapshot. The fix keeps the coordination inside the agent model catalog owner boundary and does not add config, migrations, or provider-specific policy.

## User Impact

target.title: fix: keep always-on group fallback messages in dispatch
target.body:
﻿Closes #99457

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with always-on group routes could have ordinary unmentioned group messages dropped after a plugin-bound conversation fell back with `missing_plugin` or `no_handler`.

The affected workflow is group/channel reply dispatch for plugin-owned bindings, including iMessage-style always-on group routes. Mention-required groups should still stay quiet for unmentioned chatter, but always-on groups should continue into the normal agent dispatch path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin-bound fallback branch was checking only the raw `WasMentioned === false` flag before returning. This change reuses the existing `resolveGroupRequireMention(...)` policy resolver before suppressing an unmentioned group/channel fallback, so the early return only applies when the effective group policy actually requires a mention.

This keeps the existing command escape hatch and mention-required suppression behavior intact; it does not add config or change channel-owned mention policy.

Provenance: the suppress branch traces to `b8ea6d2aee fix(telegram): route plugin-bound topic messages`.

## User Impact

Always-on group routes can now preserve unmentioned plugin-bound fallback messages in the agent/session path instead of silently dropping them. Mention-required groups continue to suppress ordinary unmentioned messages.

## Real Behavior Proof

Behavior addressed: An unmentioned group message in an always-on route (`requireMention=false`) with a plugin-owned conversation binding and a targeted plugin fallback (`no_handler`) now reaches the normal agent dispatch path instead of being suppressed by the plugin-bound fallback early return.
