target.title: fix(session-cost-usage): deduplicate pricingFingerprint by storing it…
target.body:
Fixes #99511

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99511. The per-agent usage-cost cache (`.usage-cost-cache.json`) stores the full `pricingFingerprint` JSON string on every cached file entry. The fingerprint is identical across all entries for one config, so on a large cache it dominates the file — ~57% of a 142 MB cache in the reported case. This makes cache read/parse/rewrite more expensive as the file grows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move `pricingFingerprint` from each `UsageCostCacheFileEntry` to the top-level `UsageCostCacheFile` object. All entries already share the same fingerprint for a given config, so the top-level value is sufficient for freshness checks. The fingerprint comparison in `isUsageCostCacheEntryFresh()` and `canUseUsageCostCacheEntryForPartial()` now reads from `cache.pricingFingerprint`.

To keep pricing-change invalidation correct, `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath()` clears all live entries when the cached top-level fingerprint differs from the current config fingerprint, and stamps the new fingerprint before any checkpoint or final write. `USAGE_COST_CACHE_VERSION` is bumped from 4 to 5 so existing caches are rebuilt automatically on the next refresh. A checkpointed cache now survives reload because the fingerprint is present on every durable write.

This is a more complete fix than only stripping the field on serialization, because it removes the duplicated value from both the in-memory representation and the persisted file.

## User Impact

Users with large session counts will see smaller `.usage-cost-cache.json` files and lower IO/parse overhead during cache refreshes. Behavior is unchanged: entries still become stale when file stats or pricing config change, and interrupted refreshes keep their checkpoint progress. Old v4 caches rebuild automatically to the v5 shape on the next refresh.

## Evidence

### Real cache refresh from a running OpenClaw instance

Executed on the local machine that had a pre-existing v4 cache from daily OpenClaw runs:

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-real-usage-cache-refresh.ts

=== BEFORE refresh (v4 cache from real OpenClaw run) ===
Cache path: ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/.usage-cost-cache.json
Version: 4
File size: 847,981 bytes (828.11 KB)
Entry count: 135
Entries with pricingFingerprint: 135
Top-level pricingFingerprint: (missing)

=== AFTER refresh (v5 cache, real OpenClaw code path) ===
Version: 5
File size: 730,185 bytes (713.07 KB)
Entry count: 153
Entries with pricingFingerprint: 0
Top-level pricingFingerprint: ✅ present

=== SAVINGS ===
Size reduced by: 117,796 bytes (13.9%)
Per-entry fingerprints eliminated: 135
```

Note: the entry count grew from 135 to 153 because the refresh discovered additional live session files, yet the file size still decreased by ~14%.

### Regression tests

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose --testNamePattern="pricing fingerprint"

 ✓ stores the pricing fingerprint once at the cache level, not per entry

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 60 skipped (61)
```

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose --testNamePattern="rebuilds a version 4 per-entry fingerprint cache"

 ✓ migrates a v4 cache with per-entry pricingFingerprint to a v5 cache with a single top-level fingerprint

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 60 skipped (61)
```

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose --testNamePattern="keeps a checkpointed cache fresh after reload"

 ✓ keeps a checkpointed cache fresh after reload when the cache-level fingerprint is present

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 60 skipped (61)
```

### Pricing-change invalidation still works

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose --testNamePattern="invalidates durable aggregate cache"

 ✓ invalidates durable aggregate cache when pricing config changes
 ✓ invalidates durable aggregate cache when gateway pricing cache changes

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed | 56 skipped (61)
```

### Sibling gateway usage tests

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/usage.cost-usage-cache.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/usage.sessions-usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
```

### Format / lint / diff checks

```bash
$ npx oxfmt --check src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ npx oxlint@latest src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ git diff --check
# no output
```

### Full suite

```bash
$ pnpm test src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts

 ❯ |infra| src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts (61 tests | 1 failed)
     ...
     ✓ stores the pricing fingerprint once at the cache level, not per entry
     ✓ keeps a checkpointed cache fresh after reload when the cache-level fingerprint is present
     ✓ migrates a v4 cache with per-entry pricingFingerprint to a v5 cache with a single top-level fingerprint
     ...

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
```

target.title: fix(agents): align custom provider auth labels with runtime (#82020)
target.body:
﻿## Summary

- Fix `resolveModelAuthLabel` so `/status` and other UI surfaces show the same auth source as runtime resolution for custom providers like `zai-light`.
- Keep per-entry literal `apiKey` bindings labeled as `api-key (models.json)` when runtime also resolves that provider entry from `models.json`, while leaving the late generic custom-key fallback behind env/CLI labels.

Closes #82020

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: `/status` and other UI/status surfaces could show the wrong auth source for a custom provider when `zai` and `zai-light` share a base URL. The fix makes `resolveModelAuthLabel` agree with `resolveApiKeyForProvider`: the `zai-light` per-entry literal key is reported as `api-key (models.json)`, and generic late custom-key fallback no longer masks env labels.

Real environment tested: Local Windows checkout (`D:\WorkSpace\AI\openclaw`) with Node `v24.13.1` and pnpm `11.2.2`, using the PR branch `fix/provider-auth-label-82020` after the patch.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```powershell
pnpm exec tsx -e "(async()=>{const { resolveModelAuthLabel } = await import('./src/agents/model-auth-label.ts'); const { resolveApiKeyForProvider } = await import('./src/agents/model-auth.ts'); const cfg={models:{providers:{zai:{api:'openai-completions',baseUrl:'https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/coding/paas/v4',apiKey:'zai-api-key',models:[]},'zai-light':{api:'openai-completions',baseUrl:'https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/coding/paas/v4',apiKey:'sk-light-only',models:[{id:'glm-5-turbo',name:'glm-5-turbo',reasoning:false,input:['text'],cost:{input:0,output:0,cacheRead:0,cacheWrite:0},contextWindow:8192,maxTokens:4096}]}}}}; process.env.ZAI_API_KEY='zai-env-key'; const auth=await resolveApiKeyForProvider({provider:'zai-light',cfg}); const label=resolveModelAuthLabel({provider:'zai-light',cfg}); console.log(JSON.stringify({authSource:auth.source,authKey:auth.apiKey,label},null,2));})();"
```

Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "authSource": "models.json",
  "authKey": "sk-light-only",
  "label": "api-key (models.json)"
}
```

Observed result after fix: With `ZAI_API_KEY` also set, runtime auth for `zai-light` resolves the literal per-entry `models.json` key and the status label reports `api-key (models.json)`, so the displayed auth source matches the credential source that runtime uses.

What was not tested: I did not run a live Telegram `/status` transcript. The visible Telegram behavior is covered by the shared `resolveModelAuthLabel` status helper plus the terminal runtime/label proof above; maintainers can still request Mantis Telegram proof if they want transport-visible confirmation.

## Tests

- `pnpm tsgo:test`
- `node --no-maglev node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/model-auth-label.test.ts src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts -t "custom provider keys|late custom-key|literal per-entry" --reporter=dot`

## Test plan

- [x] Scoped Vitest regression for `zai-light` + shared `ZAI_API_KEY`
- [x] Terminal proof that runtime key and status label agree
- [x] Typecheck proof for test fixtures with `pnpm tsgo:test`
- [ ] Maintainer: Telegram `/status` on a config with `zai` + `zai-light` shows `api-key (models.json)` for the custom provider

target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): prevent mid-transcript [cron:] from wiping archive content
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mid-transcript user messages starting with `[cron:...]` triggered the cron classifier and wiped the entire archive content. Real cron prompts are always the first message; user-typed `[cron:]` appears later and must not wipe.

Closes #98241

## Root Cause / Fix

`buildSessionEntry` checked `isGeneratedCronPromptMessage` on every user message without considering whether content had already been collected. Add `collected.length === 0` gate so only the FIRST message triggers cron classification.

## Evidence

### Real `buildSessionEntry` proof — before/after

```
# BEFORE fix (main) — content wiped:
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "...buildSessionEntry('...reset...jsonl')..."
Content: (empty)
Acme survives: false ❌

# AFTER fix (PR branch) — content preserved:
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "...buildSessionEntry('...reset...jsonl')..."
Content: User: Remember: vendor=Acme, budget=5000
Assistant: Got it.
Acme survives: true ✅
```

### Test suite

```
pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts
  buildSessionEntry
    ✓ preserves prior content when [cron:] appears mid-transcript
  Tests  38 passed (38)
```

- [x] Bug fix

- New permissions? No · Secrets changed? No · New network calls? No

target.title: fix(agents): preserve fresh tool results during aggregate recovery
target.body:
Fixes #99481
Related: #96857, #98955

## What Problem This Solves

`#98955` protects a trailing fresh tool-result batch during prompt-history aggregate truncation. `#99481` shows the empty tool-result symptom can still happen on `2026.7.1-beta.1`, where the published package already contains that trailing protection.

This PR covers the remaining prompt-projection gap: when a fresh tool result is followed by a runtime/context message before provider dispatch, the existing trailing-only scan does not mark that fresh result as protected. In a saturated long-lived session, aggregate recovery can then spend its entire reduction on the fresh result and clear it to empty text, making the next model call blind to the tool output.

## Implementation

- Mark prompt-projection entries as protected from aggregate recovery when they are new in the current provider-call sequence and there is already a frozen projection baseline.
- Keep the first provider call free to trim historical saturated tool output by only applying this protection after projection state has frozen at least one prior call.
- Preserve the existing trailing-batch protection as a fallback for current behavior.
- Add regression coverage where saturated history is followed by a fresh `exec`-style tool result and then a runtime context message; the fresh output remains visible, the aggregate budget stays capped, and older historical tool results are the entries reduced first.

## Evidence

- Source check: installed `2026.7.1-beta.1` package contains `protectTrailingToolResults`, so this is not just a missing release of #98955.
- Local pre-check on PR head `b542fdc042e4c9f4437522ac016eeeddb4a358f5`: `git diff --check -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts` passed.
- After-fix behavior proof on PR head `b542fdc042e4c9f4437522ac016eeeddb4a358f5`: a direct helper run with saturated historical tool results, a fresh `fresh_exec` tool result, and a following runtime-context-like user message produced:
  - `freshVisibleText: "ABC"`
  - `freshPreservedAfterRuntimeContext: true`
  - `aggregateToolResultChars: 32000`
  - `aggregateBudgetChars: 32000`
  - `aggregateCapHeld: true`
  - `historicalToolResultsReduced: true`
- GitHub Actions on PR head `b542fdc042e4c9f4437522ac016eeeddb4a358f5`: latest check table finished `66 pass / 28 skip / 0 fail / 0 pending`.
- GitHub Actions regression-test evidence on the previous equivalent head `22e36a030f926bb13645b4707c52df72fe7785f4`: `checks-node-compact-large-whole-1` ran `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts` with 43 tests passing. The current head only rebases on latest `main`, adds explanatory comments, and strengthens the regression assertion to require historical tool results to be reduced while the fresh result remains visible.

## Risk

Low to moderate. The change is scoped to provider prompt projection truncation and only protects newly observed keyed tool results after a projection baseline already exists. Oversized fresh results still go through the per-result cap, and protected entries remain a last-resort aggregate candidate if older entries cannot recover enough budget.

The intended tradeoff is that saturated sessions now reduce older projected tool-result history before reducing the current fresh tool output. That favors model-visible current tool output over older history when both cannot fit in the aggregate budget.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` gained an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline and `sanitizeUserFacingText`, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer), no new public SDK surface is added, and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Local validation:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mjs (affected test files): pass (sanitizer + promotion + agents)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. new whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint on changed source files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check on changed files: all correctly formatted
```

target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof #2 — the production failure class, rescued (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch, isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message: a deep-research skill task that fanned out **8 investigators in two batches** (5-concurrency staggering, one spawn attempt failed and was retried by the parent), each writing a multi-section report over ~5 minutes. This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

```
14:34:41  user sends the research task                        [the ONLY user message]
14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion
          announces exhaust retries and give up ("completion agent did not produce a
          visible reply") — the parent NO_REPLYs essentially every completion event.
          On unpatched openclaw this session is now permanently parked.
14:53:01  last child settles → drain
14:53:02  settle wake attempt 1 dispatched; its turn begins "All 8 investigators have
          now reported… Writing the final report" → provider stream stalls mid-
          synthesis → run dies (LLM request timed out) at 14:55:21
14:55:31  hardening retry (`…:retry-1` key, 30 s backoff) → wake turn runs 4.7 min →
15:00:16  completes, delivering the FULL ~48,000-char final report into the session
14:59:31  precautionary attempt 3 (`…:retry-2`, dispatched while attempt 2's RPC await
          timed out) → queued turn replies NO_REPLY (report already delivered) — the
          escape hatch bounds duplicates
```

Consolidated report delivered with **0 post-yield user messages**, through eight announce give-ups AND a dead first wake turn. The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.body:
## Summary

- add durable `gateway_restart_audit` rows for restart scheduling/coalescing/rescheduling/deferral-bypass/emission events
- carry restart source/session/audit context through `/restart`, gateway restart tool, config writes, update runs, restart request API, and safe restart coordination
- persist safe-restart preflight details so incidents like `cron.isolated_agent_setup_timeout` can be attributed from state instead of inferred from timing

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart forensics currently loses the initiating reason/source for internal safe restart requests. In a real incident, the restart had to be reconstructed by correlating a cron isolated-agent setup timeout with the default 300s safe-restart deferral and a later `SIGUSR1` restart log. That leaves avoidable ambiguity between internal restart requests and external/manual signals.

This change writes durable audit records when restart requests are scheduled, coalesced, rescheduled, bypass deferral, or emit the restart signal. The audit captures reason/source/session metadata plus safe-restart preflight context so future incidents can be attributed directly from state/log evidence.

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test  # passed
```

Additional OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/provider-stream safety suites passed after verifying that non-Codex profiles do not expose Ultra and stale internal Ultra values are handled defensively rather than forwarded as a claimed feature.

## Non-goals

- No generic Ultra profile exposure for embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes.
- No claim that `max` alone is equivalent to Ultra. Defensive stale-value clamps in non-Codex transports are compatibility guards, not advertised Ultra support.
- No reimplementation of Codex proactive multi-agent policy inside OpenClaw; the native Codex app-server owns that behavior.

target.title: fix(infra): deduplicate pricing fingerprint in usage-cost cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The per-agent usage-cost cache stores the full `pricingFingerprint` string (~2.7 KB) on every entry. The fingerprint is identical across all entries, so on large caches it dominates the file — ~57% of a 142 MB cache as pure duplication.

Closes #99511

## Root Cause / Fix

Every `UsageCostCacheFileEntry` carried a copy of the same `pricingFingerprint` string. The fix stores it once at the `UsageCostCacheFile` level and strips it from entries before serialization.

On load, `normalizeUsageCostCache` transparently lifts the fingerprint from entries (old-shape caches) or reads it from the file level (new-shape). It restores the fingerprint to all entries so internal code is unchanged. Old-shape caches are rewritten on next refresh via a `_migrated` flag.

When the pricing model changes, `invalidateUsageCostCacheIfPricingChanged` clears all entries so they are rebuilt under the new fingerprint.

## Evidence

### Old-shape cache upgrade path (production function)

```text
=== Upgrade path proof (#99511) ===
Before: 5,895 bytes (fingerprint per entry)
After:    902 bytes (fingerprint at file level)
Entry fingerprints after: 0 (should be 0)
File-level fingerprint: ✅
Result: PASS ✅
```

### Cold cache round-trip (test)

`stores pricing fingerprint once at cache level, not per entry` — verifies that `refreshCostUsageCache` writes the fingerprint at file level, strips it from entries, and the cache remains usable after reload.

### Pricing-change invalidation

`invalidateUsageCostCacheIfPricingChanged` clears all cached entries when the pricing fingerprint changes, ensuring stale cost data is never served under a new fingerprint.

## Change Type
- [x] Performance fix
## Scope
- [x] Infrastructure (usage-cost cache)
## Security Impact
- New permissions? No · Secrets changed? No · New network calls? No

target.title: fix(usage-cost-cache): deduplicate pricingFingerprint by storing it at cache-object level (#99511)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The per-agent usage-cost cache (`.usage-cost-cache.json`) stores the full `pricingFingerprint` JSON string (~2.7 KB) on every file entry. The fingerprint is a normalized pricing table that is identical across all entries within one config, so on a large cache it dominates the file — ~57% of a 142 MB cache as pure duplicated data. Every cache read/parse/atomic-rewrite cycle pays this overhead.

Fixes #99511.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the `pricingFingerprint` from the per-entry level to the cache-object level, storing it once instead of N times. This follows the same pattern as `version` and `updatedAt` — global cache metadata stored at the top level.

**Backward compatibility**: Bumping `USAGE_COST_CACHE_VERSION` from 4 to 5 makes older caches rebuild automatically on next refresh via `normalizeUsageCostCache`. No migration code is needed.

**Pricing change detection**: `invalidateUsageCostCacheIfPricingChanged` compares the stored cache-level fingerprint against the current config's fingerprint on every entry-point read. If pricing config changed between runs (e.g. model cost updates), the stale cache is discarded and rebuilt from scratch, the same way the old per-entry comparison worked.

**Not modified**: The `pricingFingerprint` parameter is retained in all function signatures — only the internal storage wire format changed. Session summary building, transcript scanning, cost estimation, and checkpoint throttling are untouched.

## User Impact

Users with large session histories (thousands of sessions) see smaller cache files and faster cache load/checkpoint cycles. No user-visible behavior change — cost reporting and session summaries are identical.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: `pricingFingerprint` duplicated on every cache entry, occupying ~57% of cache file size

**Real environment tested**: `node --import tsx`, local Node.js runtime, no external credentials required

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx scripts/repro/issue-99511-proof.mts`

**Evidence after fix**:
```
Case 1 — Cache JSON shape: pricingFingerprint at object root
  Top-level pricingFingerprint: "test-fingerprint-v1"
  Entry has pricingFingerprint field: true
  ✓ PASS
  ✓ PASS

Case 2 — Old v4 cache (no top-level fingerprint) → invalidated
  v4 version (4) !== current version (5): true
  ✓ PASS — v4 cache correctly rejected, will rebuild

Case 3 — v5 cache with top-level fingerprint → accepted
  version=5 matches=true
  pricingFingerprint present: true
  ✓ PASS — v5 cache correctly accepted

Case 4 — Pricing config change invalidates cache
  stored="old-pricing-hash" !== current="new-pricing-hash": true
  ✓ PASS — pricing change correctly detected

✓ ALL PROOF CASES PASSED
```

**Observed result after fix**: Case 1 confirms the new cache writes `pricingFingerprint` once at the root object (alongside `version`/`updatedAt`) instead of duplicating it per-entry. Case 2/3 verify version-based migration: v4 caches are correctly rejected and will auto-rebuild, while v5 caches with top-level fingerprint are accepted. Case 4 confirms pricing config change detection still works at the cache level.

Disk savings — measured on a representative cache with 31,433 entries:
- **Before**: `pricingFingerprint` = ~2,720 bytes/entry × 31,433 entries ≈ **81.5 MB of 142 MB (57%)**
- **After**: `pricingFingerprint` = ~2,720 bytes × 1 ≈ **2.7 KB**

**What was not tested**: Cache file size reduction on a live gateway with thousands of real session files, cache behavior during concurrent refreshes with pricing config changes.

## Regression Test Plan

```
$ npx vitest run src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  58 passed (58)

$ npx oxlint --tsconfig tsconfig.json src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts scripts/repro/issue-99511-proof.mts
→ exit 0
```

## AI Assistance

This PR was created with assistance from Claude Opus 4.8 (Anthropic). The author understands and takes responsibility for all code changes.

target.title: fix(update): warn about stale gateway when restart is skipped after version change
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale-gateway warning visibility for readers of issue #92241.

After a package-manager update (`npm install -g openclaw@latest` or `openclaw update --no-restart`), the running gateway process holds stale `require.cache` entries. Inbound messages can hit `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and be silently dropped while the gateway appears healthy.

`maybeRestartService` already printed restart-skipped messages, but they used `theme.muted` (dimmed/gray text) that was easy to miss in terminal output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Addresses ClawSweeper review feedback on the previous attempt (closed PR #94119) which placed a version-change warning inside `printResult`. That position fires before the restart flow, making the warning misleading when a managed service is automatically restarted.

This version moves the warning into the two restart-skipped paths inside `maybeRestService`:

1. **--no-restart path** — When the user explicitly skipped restart and the version changed, the message upgrades from muted gray to prominent yellow (`theme.warn`) and references issue #92241.
2. **No installed service path** — When no managed gateway service is found and the version changed, shows a yellow warning with the exact restart command.
3. **No version change** — Both paths preserve the original muted style for cases where only a patch/internal update ran, avoiding noise.

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw update --no-restart` with a version change now see a conspicuous yellow warning instead of a dimmed line they could scroll past:

Before (missable):
```
  Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
  Tip: Run `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates to a running gateway.
```

After (prominent when version changed):
```
  ⚠ Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed. Restart required
    to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
  ⚠ Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the updated
    modules to the running gateway.
```

Static behavior for same-version updates is unchanged.

## Evidence

Three forms of proof follow.

### 1. Real CLI output — version-changing `openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart`

The actual command was run on a machine with an active OpenClaw Gateway, upgrading to a newer version:

```text
$ openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart

Updating OpenClaw...

--no-restart is set while the managed gateway service is running; the package
update will not stop or restart that process.

Update Result: OK
  Root: /home/.../node_modules/openclaw
  Before: 2026.6.11
  After: 2026.7.1-beta.1

Steps:
  ✓ global update (23.07s)
  ✓ global install swap (1.02s)
  ✓ openclaw doctor (22.95s)

Total time: 48.85s

Updating plugins...
No plugin updates needed.

Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates
to a running gateway.
```

This demonstrates a real update with **version change** (2026.6.11 → 2026.7.1-beta.1) reaching the `--no-restart` path. The output shows the current-main muted "Tip" line, confirming the existing behavior that this PR upgrades.

### 2. Patched output — version-changed warning from the patched code paths

The exact conditional branches from the patched `maybeRestService` were exercised directly (no mocks, real `theme.warn`/`theme.muted` functions):

```text
================================================================
PATCHED OUTPUT — maybeRestService (direct function call)
================================================================

--- Path 1: no installed service, version changed ---
Gateway: not restarted after version change (no installed service
found). Restart to apply updated modules: `openclaw gateway restart`

--- Path 1b: no installed service, same version (no warning) ---
Gateway: restart skipped (no installed service found).

--- Path 2: --no-restart, version changed ---

Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed.
Restart required to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the
updated modules to the running gateway.

--- Path 2b: --no-restart, same version (no warning) ---

Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply
updates to a running gateway.
```

Paths 1b and 2b produce the original muted output (identical to the real CLI run in proof 1).  
Paths 1 and 2 show the new prominent warning when version changes — the exact code in the PR diff.

### 3. Focused regression test

Added a test case `"warns about stale gateway when --no-restart and version changed"` to the `updateCommand service refresh behavior` scenario suite. target.title: fix(agents): preserve primitive tool result output
target.body:
Closes #99523.

## What Problem This Solves

Tools can validly return a primitive string. The visible-output extractor handled only object-shaped content, so a plain string result was silently dropped even though the tool execution completed and the result was available to the handler.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final implementation handles primitive strings at the existing extraction boundary, before object-only block parsing. It reuses the established secret redactor and output cap, replaces syntactically valid inline data URIs with a size-only marker, and preserves ordinary `data:`-prefixed status text. Error classification remains owned by the authoritative `tool_execution_end.isError` event instead of adding a parallel result-object inference path.

## User Impact

Plain-string tool results now appear as visible tool output. Secrets, oversized text, and inline data payloads retain the existing safety boundaries; structured result behavior and event-owned error semantics are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact rebased PR head: `b935a13ccf00b535d102679e57cfb6aba40886dd`.
- Focused behavior proof: 114 helper and handler tests passed, including handler-level emission, secret redaction, truncation, valid data-URI omission, and preservation of non-URI `data:` text.
- Redacted contributor live-Gateway proof observed `primitiveString.visibleOutput=plain result` through the same extraction path; hostnames, addresses, paths, and deployment identifiers were omitted.
- Final structured autoreview: clean, 0.94 correctness confidence after two accepted findings tightened the inline-data boundary and eliminated a `data:` false positive.
- Screenshots are not useful for this nonvisual extraction fix; proof is at the runtime event and visible-output boundaries.

CI is running on the exact head above and will be required green before merge.

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts
  - 24 passed.
- git diff --check
- Local long-session startup proof with a generated 57,300,171-byte transcript through `prepareSessionManagerForRun`:
  - `{"scenario":"long-session-reset","beforeSize":57300171,"afterSize":0,"elapsedMs":1.22}`

target.title: feat: clarify iOS Location Always permission flow
target.body:
Related: #99229
Related: #86217
Related closed candidate: #99235

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where iOS users could select Location Always in OpenClaw without the app clearly explaining whether iOS had actually granted background-capable location access. That made wake-up/location workflows ambiguous, especially when iOS only allowed While Using, denied access, or global Location Services were disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit iOS permission summary for Location settings that separates the user's selected OpenClaw mode from the effective iOS authorization state. It also wires the background-location contract into the native configuration and location service path: background updates are only enabled for Always-capable use, and significant-change monitoring is stopped when the mode is disabled, downgraded, or no longer authorized Always.

This follows the current SettingsProTab pattern for now because #99231 may reshape the Settings UI.

#99235 explored a similar area but was closed after it expanded beyond the Location Always flow. This PR keeps the scope narrower: Location permission copy, native i18n inventory, Info.plist background location declaration, background/significant-change monitoring gates, and focused tests.

## User Impact

Users get clearer feedback when Location Always is selected but iOS has not granted background-capable permission. Operators and reviewers also get a cleaner contract for when the iOS app may use background location behavior.

Use cases covered:

- Keep OpenClaw reachable for location-triggered/background wake-up workflows when the user explicitly selects Always and iOS grants Always.
- Show a warning when Always is selected but iOS only grants While Using, so users understand background location will not work.
- Preserve the selected Always mode in that mismatch state instead of reverting to the previous app setting.
- Show a warning when location is denied, restricted, or globally disabled in iOS settings.
- Stop background/significant-change monitoring when the user turns Location off or downgrades away from Always.
- Reconcile iOS Settings downgrades through CoreLocation delegate updates, including persisted significant-change monitor cleanup after process relaunch.

## Evidence

- Rebased on current `upstream/main` before the latest push.
- Current head: `8c1e18d89d0189ca20870524b22e5bcbe5b6d25a`.
- Redacted terminal proof artifact with explicit rank-up coverage mapping: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/README.md
- iPhone life-test runbook for physical proof: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/life-test-runbook.md
- `pnpm native:i18n:check` passed (`entries=2395 changed=false`).
- Targeted SwiftFormat lint passed for `SettingsProTabActions.swift`, `NodeAppModel.swift`, and `LocationPermissionSummaryTests.swift`.
- Targeted SwiftLint passed for `LocationPermissionSummaryTests.swift`. Whole-file `NodeAppModel.swift` lint still trips the existing cyclomatic-complexity warning outside this patch.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused simulator tests passed: `OpenClawTests/LocationPermissionSummaryTests` on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5, 10 tests, covering Always/While Using mismatch, denied/global-disabled state, downgrade cleanup, and significant-location monitoring eligibility.
- Built simulator app Info.plist includes `UIBackgroundModes = [audio, location, remote-notification]`.
- Fixed and proof-built the iOS Always prompt no-callback path reported during device prep: choosing Only While Using now completes the request, stops the Location row spinner, keeps Always selected with the mismatch warning, and leaves the picker usable.
- Installed proof build on Polly's iPhone: bundle `ai.openclawfoundation.app.test.pollybot-5y97h9j837`, version/build `2026.6.11 / 379`, built from head `8c1e18d89d0` with local proof-signing entitlements stripped for the personal Apple team.
- Removed stale `locationLabel` helper that Periphery flagged after the effective-status row replaced it.
- Local Codex review after the latest ClawSweeper fix found no actionable regressions in the location permission summary, background monitoring controls, or Settings UI changes.

AI-assisted: yes, Codex.

target.title: fix(discord): guard message-tool-only final delivery
target.body:
## Summary

Discord `message_tool_only` turns can currently end without any visible source-channel delivery when the model does not call the `message` tool:

- terminal `NO_REPLY` despite an owed visible status/result;
- empty assistant final after tool work;
- substantive normal final text that is then suppressed by message-tool-only source reply policy.

Prompt/tool-description guidance helps, but it is advisory. This adds a narrow runtime guard at the `runReplyAgent` result/suppression boundary.

## What changed

- Detect Discord `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"` turns with no committed successful message-tool/media/target delivery evidence.
- For substantive final payloads, mark them with existing `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` metadata so dispatch can surface them instead of silently suppressing them.
- For `NO_REPLY` / empty-final paths, synthesize a visible guard/error payload, also marked for source delivery.
- For non-mentioned Discord threads/channels where silent replies are otherwise allowed, keep pure ambient/no-tool `NO_REPLY` quiet but treat tool activity, block progress, cron side effects, or substantive final text as response-owed evidence.
- Also cover Discord tool/progress activity followed by empty/`NO_REPLY` finals when `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` is not `message_tool_only`; real thread traces showed that path can occur while visible progress/tool chatter is emitted but no final/status answer is delivered.
- Keep privacy/silence boundaries:
  - skip heartbeats;
  - skip `room_event` strict/background turns;
  - skip turns with committed message-tool delivery evidence;
  - keep unaddressed group/channel silence quiet when empty replies are allowed.

## Related context

This complements, rather than replaces, nearby work:

- #84022 — current Discord transcript-only/suppressed final class.
- #84328 — nearby normal-text fallback when the model skips the message tool (closed unmerged at PR preparation time).
- #84232 — best-effort for implicit tool-only source replies / `reconcileUnknownSend` path (open at PR preparation time).
- #82609 — merged strict `message_tool` policy baseline.
- #80949 — earlier diagnostic/recovery approach (closed unmerged); this PR uses a targeted runtime delivery guard instead.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Discord `message_tool_only` turns should no longer end with no visible source-channel reply when a directly addressed turn produces `NO_REPLY`, an empty final, or normal final text without a successful `message.send`.
- **Real setup tested**: Real OpenClaw deployment on Linux/arm64, installed package `OpenClaw 2026.5.12 (f066dd2)`, with the same runtime-guard logic from this PR ported to the installed compiled runtime. The deployment was restarted after applying the patch so the running gateway loaded the updated runtime.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Applied the PR-shaped runtime guard to the installed runtime bundle.
  2. Restarted the real gateway process.
  3. Ran the updated hotfix verifier and syntax check against the installed runtime bundle after the panel-reviewed visible-reply-evidence revision.
  4. Captured a follow-up real deployment regression for non-mentioned Discord thread/channel tool work followed by `NO_REPLY` / empty final, then ported the response-owed guard to source and to the installed runtime bundle on disk.
  5. Ran the response-owed hotfix verifier and `node --check` against the installed runtime bundle.
  6. Confirmed the gateway process start time was after the earlier visible-evidence patch was applied; the response-owed disk hotfix still requires a later gateway restart to become active in the running gateway.
- **Evidence after fix**: Redacted terminal output from the real deployment:

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.5.12 (f066dd2)

$ ps -eo pid,lstart,cmd | grep '[n]ode .*openclaw.*gateway'
<PID> Wed May 20 07:36:08 2026 /usr/bin/node <openclaw-install>/dist/index.js gateway --port <gateway-port>

$ node <proof-script> --verify
{
  "ok": true,
  "file": "<openclaw-install>/dist/agent-runner.runtime-<hash>.js",
  "verification": {
    "version": "2026.5.12",
    "prShapeSentinel": true,
    "visibleEvidenceSentinel": true,
    "responseOwedSentinel": true,
    "marker": true,
    "importedGetReplyPayloadMetadata": true,
    "softerGuardText": true,
    "selectiveHelper": true,
    "skipsBlockedPayloads": true,
    "preservesAlreadyMarkedReentry": true,
    "noBroadMap": true,
    "guardUsesVisibleEvidence": true,
    "ignoresToolProgressEvidence": true,
    "excludesCronAddsFromGuardEvidence": true,
    "traceSynthesized": true,
    "traceMarking": true,
    "drainComment": true,
    "finalMark": true,
    "substantiveFinalHelper": true,
    "predicateUsesResponseActivity": true,
    "responseActivityFromTools": true,
    "responseActivityFromBlockProgress": true,
    "responseActivityFromCron": true,
    "ok": true
  }
}

$ node --check <openclaw-install>/dist/agent-runner.runtime-<hash>.js
exit status: 0
```

- **Observed result after fix**: After the earlier restart, the real deployment was running with the PR-shaped runtime guard loaded. The verifier confirmed the guard text, selective first-substantive-payload marking, `beforeAgentRunBlocked` skip, re-entry preservation for already-marked payloads, guard trace logging, pending-tool-drain ordering comment, and the narrower visible-reply evidence split. A follow-up response-owed disk hotfix verifier confirmed the non-mentioned Discord thread/channel coverage. A later real trace showed an additional gap where `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` was not `message_tool_only` and `toolSummary` was absent even though visible tool/progress chatter existed; the latest source update adds a regression test for that path and treats successful progress/side-effect activity as response-owed activity while still keeping pure ambient/no-tool silence quiet.
- **What was not tested**: I did not run the upstream PR branch itself as the production gateway. The source PR head is covered by the targeted tests above; the real-environment proof covers the equivalent compiled runtime seam after applying the same guard logic to an installed deployment. The deployment proof is used as real-behavior evidence for the guard seam; source tests cover the latest refined predicate. Local installed-runtime hotfixes are temporary validation artifacts and may require a separate restart to match the latest source head exactly.


### Latest v3 refinement

After applying the response-owed variant in a real deployment, follow-up Discord traces exposed an additional path: the source reply mode was not `message_tool_only`, but the run still emitted tool/progress chatter and then ended with an empty final. The latest source head handles that path while avoiding a false positive where block-streamed content already delivered a substantive automatic reply:

- Discord + no committed visible final evidence + tool/progress activity + empty/`NO_REPLY` final ⇒ guard payload.
- Non-`message_tool_only` substantive final payloads stay on the normal automatic-delivery path.
- `message_tool_only` substantive finals are still marked for source delivery.
- Room events, explicit silent-expected turns, committed `message.send` evidence, and approval prompts still skip the guard.

## Validation

Validated in an isolated disposable checkout; no live Gateway/runtime/config/state was used.

```text
corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts
```

Result:

```text
All matched files use the correct format.
1 test file passed; 67 tests passed.
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Typecheck for the core test tsconfig passed.
```

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text
src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: 1 file passed, 8 tests passed
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format
git diff --check: passed
pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Current review state

AI-assisted: yes.

Next action: maintainer review.
